questions.prompt: What does Chapter 10 say culture really is?
choices: A mood layer around the real work
A productive form of alignment that changes execution
A set of perks that keeps morale high

explanation.gentle: The chapter treats culture as part of how work actually gets done.
explanation.direct: Its definition is productive alignment, not mood or perks.
explanation.competitive: Culture matters when it changes motion, not just atmosphere.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter care so much about mission fit?
choices: Because shared purpose matters more than prestige alone
Because talent is never useful
Because culture is mainly social chemistry

explanation.gentle: The chapter says people need to care about the same mission deeply enough to reinforce one another.
explanation.direct: Mission fit matters because an aligned team is stronger than a merely impressive one.
explanation.competitive: Prestige does not compound if the mission pull is weak.

questions.prompt: What limit keeps this chapter from collapsing into fluff?
choices: Culture is just friendship
Perks and atmosphere can substitute for trust
Real culture is about productive fit, not startup-family theater

explanation.gentle: The chapter rejects perk talk and vague family language as substitutes for real fit.
explanation.direct: Its limit is that culture matters through mission, trust, and role clarity in the work itself.

questions.prompt: Nolan has a skilled team that still does not compound well. Which lesson fits best?
choices: Talent alone may not be enough without mission fit
Perks should be increased first
The team should ignore culture and focus only on output

explanation.gentle: The chapter says weak mission fit can keep strong people from reinforcing one another.
explanation.direct: Nolan is facing a culture problem at the level of alignment, not raw ability.
explanation.competitive: The room has skill, but not enough shared pull.

questions.prompt: Why is the more aligned candidate often stronger than the more impressive candidate in founder club?
choices: Because credentials never matter
Because selection shapes future execution quality
Because friendship is the main test

explanation.gentle: The chapter says who joins shapes whether the team becomes coherent.
explanation.direct: Selection is a design choice about how the company will actually work.
explanation.competitive: A flashy hire can still be a structural downgrade.

questions.prompt: How does trust become productive in this chapter?
choices: By creating lower drag and cleaner coordination
By making difficult conversations unnecessary
By replacing the need for role clarity

explanation.gentle: The chapter links trust to better coordination and lower internal friction.
explanation.direct: Trust matters operationally because it supports cleaner execution.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter reject perks and vibe-talk as the core of culture?
choices: Because office design is always harmful
Because decorative signals are weak substitutes for real fit
Because social connection never matters

explanation.gentle: The chapter says culture matters when mission, trust, and roles reinforce the work itself.
explanation.direct: Perks and atmosphere can decorate a team without making it more coherent.

questions.prompt: Mia is choosing between a high-status team and a more aligned one. What would Chapter 10 tell her to prioritize?
choices: Status, because it attracts more talent later
Mission fit and productive role coherence
Whichever group seems friendlier

explanation.gentle: The chapter treats productive alignment as more important than prestige alone.
explanation.direct: Mia should judge the teams by fit for the real work, not by outside shine.
explanation.competitive: Pick the crew that compounds, not the badge that sparkles.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 10 connect culture and performance?
choices: A close team always wins because it is emotionally warm
Shared mission and trust reduce internal waste and improve execution
Culture matters only after product-market fit

explanation.gentle: The chapter says a well-matched team works better, not merely feels closer.
explanation.direct: It links culture to output through lower drag and stronger coordination.
explanation.competitive: A coherent crew leaks less force.
